Subject: Private Offer: NimbusAI - AWS Marketplace (rev-share & term request)

Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood for inference in our product. Procurement asked me to kick off the private offer request so we can buy via AWS Marketplace (our standard for vendor procurement). A few asks from our side: 

- We need an 18-month term (they want 12 + optional 6-month extension baked into the private offer)
- We are requesting a 25% list discount from Redwood list for the private offer price
- We expect the marketplace rev-share to be 15% (we typically see vendors accept 15% so it doesn’t come out of our negotiated price)
- Annual billing in advance preferred, with a committed minimum of $250k for year 1

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate these terms? Procurement needs a rough yes/no by Monday 2/23 to keep timing for our board approval. I’ve attached our SOW and procurement checklist. 

Best,
Claire

Team — forwarding Nimbus procurement request. Key asks summarized below (original message attached):

- Laura — this is a likely expansion/enterprise logo. Recommend escalation path? Do you want me to propose an alternate concession (e.g., keep rev-share 20% but offer 22% discount)?

Subject: Re: Fwd: Private Offer: NimbusAI - AWS Marketplace (rev-share & term request)

Jordan / team — I ran a quick sensitivity model (attached: financial_impact.xlsx). High level: 

- Baseline: 12-month term, 20% discount cap, 20% marketplace rev-share -> gross margin ~ 68% (after platform & hosting costs)
- Customer ask: 18-month term + 25% discount + 15% rev-share -> gross margin drops to ~58% (material impact for a committed deal of $250k)

Observations and recommendation: 
- The revenue certainty of 18 months helps cash flow if prepay occurs, but the 25% discount + reduced rev-share (15%) shifts economics unfavorably because AWS rev-share typically is applied to the private-offer price — if they want the rev-share to be lower, that effectively increases our net proceeds but only if AWS agrees.
- I prefer holding rev-share at 20% (our standard) and negotiating discount to 20% max; that keeps margin above 63% which is acceptable. If marketing/sales want to grant extra 5% discount (25% total), this requires CFO/CEO approval due to margin impact.

Action: if Sales wants to accept the full ask (25% + 15% rev-share), escalate to exec approvals (request to CEO + CFO). If Sales accepts my alternative (20% rev-share / 20% discount) we are fine to proceed with deal desk approval only.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Finance 
Attachment: financial_impact.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>; vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com; laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private Offer: NimbusAI - AWS Marketplace (rev-share & term request)

Thanks — quick legal read. A few items to flag: 

- 18-month term: fine from a contract perspective but we should include a 30-day early-exit for material breach and clarify indemnities; we should not agree to auto-renew without notice.
- Prepay: include refund/clawback language if we fail to deliver SLA thresholds that matter to them; otherwise procurement will push back.
- Marketplace rev-share ask: need clarity whether AWS will accept a 15% rev-share on our private offer (AWS sets the marketplace fee; vendors typically absorb that). If AWS requires 20% we need to price accordingly.

I edited the procurement redlines and attached a doc (procurement_redlines.docx) with inline comments. From a legal risk standpoint, approving an unusual rev-share + deep discount together increases exposure (makes us dependent on the private-offer billing path). If Sales wants to proceed with the full concessions, require sign-off from GC + CFO + CEO and include conservative termination triggers and audit rights.

Marissa Cole
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: procurement_redlines.docx
From: AWS Marketplace <aws-mp@amazon.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>; Claire Summers <claire.summers@nimbus.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer setup: NimbusAI / Redwood

Jordan / Claire — quick note from AWS Marketplace ops: we can create a private offer for NimbusAI once the vendor (Redwood) confirms the private-offer price and the marketplace fee split. A few clarifications: 

- Standard marketplace fee is 20%. AWS can consider a fee adjustment for case-by-case partners, but that requires approval and sometimes a revenue-share commitment timeline; 15% is not typical and will add latency to setup.
- Private offers support non-standard terms (length and billing cadence) but you must ensure the final offer price accounts for marketplace fee.
- For a smooth path, provide a final price file and the signed private-offer agreement via our portal link: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/priv-offers/12345.

If Redwood confirms it will accept 20% fee and signs the private-offer request, we can provision the offer in ~3 business days. If you need us to pursue a reduced-fee exception, we can route but estimate 2-3 weeks for review.

Thanks,
AWS Marketplace Ops
aws-mp@amazon.com
